title: Backward Direction: Nonderogatory Implies Cyclic Vector (Infinite Fields)

problemStatement.formal: theorem nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_infinite [Infinite K] (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) (h : IsNonderogatory M) : ∃ v, IsCyclicVector M v
problemStatement.plain: Over an infinite field K, if M is nonderogatory (minpoly = charpoly), then M has a cyclic vector v such that {v, Mv, ..., M^{n-1}v} spans K^n.
whyMatters: Eliminates the main axiom from CayleyHamiltonMinpolyOQ04.lean for all infinite fields
The proof uses a union-avoidance argument: non-cyclic vectors lie in finitely many proper subspaces, and over infinite fields these cannot cover the whole space

proven: nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_infinite: over any infinite field, nonderogatory ↔ has cyclic vector (backward direction)

insights: Key technique: non-cyclic vectors lie in ker((μ/q)(M)) for each normalized factor q of μ
Union avoidance: over infinite fields K^n cannot be a finite union of proper subspaces
GCD/Bezout: if p(M)v=0 and μ(M)=0, then gcd(p,μ)(M)v=0 by Bezout identity
Factor extraction: if gcd(p,μ) has irreducible factor q' dividing some factor of μ, contradiction with v ∉ ker((μ/q')(M))
